elders.label: Ask the Elders for the Verses

scholar.label: Scholar
scholar.blurb: No timer. Codex open during hearings.

elder.label: Elder of the Gate
elder.blurb: Timed on harder petitions; Codex closed while the clock runs. +25% renown.

shofet.label: Judge at the Gate
shofet.blurb: Every petition is timed, hints cost double and reveal less. +50% renown.

scroll.label: Scroll of the Elders
scroll.blurb: Reveals the principle and the verses for free (no score penalty).

witness.label: Second Witness
witness.blurb: Rules out one wrong ruling before you decide.

appeal.label: Appeal to the Elders
appeal.blurb: After a wrong ruling, re-judge at half credit; the penalty becomes the smaller of the two.

bands.label: Rain in Due Season
bands.narrative: Rain falls in its season and the gates are quiet. Righteous judgement has the land at peace.

bands.label: Peace Within the Gates
bands.narrative: The gate stands open. Righteous judgements foster agricultural blessing and civic peace.

bands.label: Covenant Strained
bands.narrative: Whispers of favouritism circulate. Wealthy clans now try to buy the bench.

bands.label: Land Imperilled
bands.narrative: Bloodguilt and discord stalk the land. Bribers crowd your door.

epilogues.title: A Tenure Just Begun
epilogues.text: You have sat at the gate for only {rounds} rounds. The elders are still watching to see what kind of judge you will be.

epilogues.title: Judge of All Israel
epilogues.text: After {years} years at the gate, with {accuracy}% fidelity across {judged} rulings, your name is spoken beside the great judges. Elders from distant tribes bring their hardest cases to you, and the land has known rain in due season.

epilogues.title: A Righteous Shofet
epilogues.text: Over {rounds} rounds you applied the law with a steady, honest hand ({accuracy}% fidelity). Not every ruling was perfect, but the people trusted the gate, and the land prospered.

epilogues.title: A Steady Hand at the Gate
epilogues.text: Your tenure was neither glorious nor shameful: {accuracy}% fidelity across {judged} rulings. The gate held, though the elders remember a handful of rulings they wish had gone differently.

epilogues.title: A Strained Covenant
epilogues.text: With {accuracy}% fidelity and a Standing of {standing}, your tenure left the covenant frayed. Clans learned that the gate could be pressured, and the next judge inherits a hard task.

epilogues.title: The Land Imperilled
epilogues.text: Bloodguilt and favouritism marked your years at the gate ({accuracy}% fidelity, Standing {standing}). The prophets will not remember your name kindly.

blessing.title: Righteous Ruling
blessing.effect: The people see the law applied faithfully, and trust in the gate grows.

3.title: Grave Miscarriage of Justice
3.effect: A ruling this serious shakes the people's trust in the gate and invites bloodguilt, vengeance or oppression across the tribes.

2.title: Justice Bent
2.effect: The injured party leaves unsatisfied and the guilty learn that the court can be moved; discontent spreads through the town.

1.title: Rough Justice
1.effect: The ruling is lenient or clumsy; the dispute festers and neighbours quarrel over what the law really requires.

trapNotes.ane: This is the Ancient Near Eastern answer (Hammurabi-style). The Torah deliberately breaks with it; see the comparison table in the Codex.
trapNotes.harsh: A harsher penalty than the Torah allows for this situation.
trapNotes.lenient: Too lenient: the Torah does not let this offender off so lightly.
trapNotes.feud: Blood-feud justice: the Torah replaces private vengeance with the court and the cities of refuge.
